1.

Petitioner has preferred this revision petition aggrieved by Judgment dated 08.03.2017 passed by Special Judge SC/ST (Prevention of Adulteration Cases), Ajmer in Criminal Appeal No. 08/2017 (01/2013) whereby the appellate Court dismissed the appeal and confirmed the judgment and order dated 18.12.2012 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate No.1 in Criminal Case No.
476/2009 (333/90) whereby the petitioner has been convicted for offence under Section 7/16 (1) (A)
(1) Prevention of Adulteration Act.

sentences.text:
2. It is contended by counsel for the petitioner that sample of Ghee was taken from the shop M/s.
Amolak Chand Tara Chand situated at Ghee Mandi, Madar Gate, Ajmer on 05.02.1990.

The sample was found to contain 1.2% moisture and thus adulterated as the maximum moisture percentage prescribed was 0.5%.
(2 of 3) [CRLR-420/2017]
3. It is contended that charge-sheet was filed against petitioner and his father Amolak Chand his father expired during pendency of the trial and the Court proceeded against the present petitioner.
4. It is contended that the petitioner moved the Court for sending the sample to Central Food Laboratory.
The prayer of the petitioner was allowed by the Court on 28.11.1990 and directions were given for sending the sample to Central Food Laboratory.

5. It is contended that the sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory on 25.10.2010 and a Mukesh Jain vs State Of Rajasthan Through Pp on 27 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143037797/

sentences.text: report
was submitted by the Central Food Laboratory.

6. It is contended by the counsel that the sample was sent laboratory to Central Food Laboratory after twenty years of the date of taking of sample and as such there was no justification for the Court below to place reliance on the report given by Central Food Laboratory.

It is also contended that the report of the Central Food Laboratory was not put to the petitioner under Section 313 Cr.P.C. and therefore placing conviction on the said report is perse illegal.
7. Public Prosecutor has opposed the revision petition her contention is that the sample was found to be adulterated.
8.

I have considered the contentions and have perused the impugned order passed by the Court below as well as the order passed by the appellate Court in the order passed by the trial Court, the Court has observed that the report given by State Food Laboratory looses its relevance after receipt of report from Central Food Laboratory and has convicted the petitioner on the basis of the report given by Central Food Laboratory.
9. I am of the considered view that a document which is not put to the accused and which is not Exhibited before the Court cannot form the basis of conviction of an accused.
Admittedly the samples were drawn on 05.02.1990, in spite of there being on order of the Court below dated 28.11.1990, samples were not sent to the Central Food Laboratory for twenty years.
The report received from Central Food Laboratory was neither Exhibited nor was put to the accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
The petitioner therefore did not have any opportunity to tender his explanation to the report received from Central Food Laboratory.
10. The conviction of the petitioner on the basis of report of Central Food Laboratory drawn after twenty years of drawing of sample and which was neither exhibited nor put the accused petitioner.

11. This Court could have remanded the matter for exhibiting the report and seeking explanation of the petitioner but considering the fact that samples were sent to Central Food Laboratory after twenty years and petitioner is reeling under threat of conviction for more than thirty seven years.
I deem it proper to set aside and quash the orders passed by the Court below.
12. The petition is accordingly allowed, petitioner is acquitted of the charge levelled against him.
Petitioner be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other case.
The record of the Court below be returned back forthwith.
(PANKAJ BHANDARI)J. Arun/131
